description: The OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect client for ASP.NET Core applications. One call in Program.cs plus an Authority and a ClientId, and [Authorize] works. It configures ASP.NET Core's own OpenID Connect and cookie handlers rather than hand-rolling the protocol, so PKCE, state, nonce, JWKS rollover and token refresh come from the framework. Also provides the flows outside interactive sign-in: a setup probe that checks local configuration against the provider's live metadata, the client credentials grant, and dynamic client registration (RFC 7591/7592). Built for Ark.oAuth.Oidc, but because it is the stock handler underneath, changing Authority and ClientId points the same application at Entra ID, Okta, Auth0 or Keycloak.
releaseNotes:
2.1.0 — account switching on a shared browser.

Fixes the case where two people use one browser. Single sign-on is browser-wide, so once the first
person has signed in anywhere, the provider's session answers the authorize request of every other
client in that browser. The second person opens a different application, is silently signed in as
the first, is told they do not have access — and has no way back, because the sign-in link returns
to the same session and gives the same answer.

* ark_oauth_client:AccountSwitch:RequireArkClaims moves the entitlement check to the callback. An
  account with no ark_claims for this client is refused before the authentication cookie is
  written, so the browser never holds a session for somebody who cannot use the application.
* A built-in access-denied page at /ark/no-access names the account that is signed in and offers
  "Sign in as a different user", which challenges with prompt=login so the provider draws its
  sign-in form instead of answering from its session. It also replaces the framework's
  /Account/AccessDenied default for ordinary [Authorize] 403s, which most applications never
  create and which therefore renders as a 404.
* HttpContext.ArkSwitchUserAsync / ArkSignOutEverywhereAsync / ArkSignOutLocallyAsync, and
  ArkChallengeProperties.SwitchUser for a challenge you issue yourself — prompt, login_hint and
  max_age now reach the authorize request through the authentication properties.
* An AddArkOidcClient(configuration, options) overload carrying ArkClientEvents: OnEvaluateAccess
  for an entitlement rule of your own, OnAccessDenied to log it or render your own page.

The page and its two POST endpoints register themselves, so Program.cs needs no edit. Every part is
off or unchanged by default: consumers on 2.0.3 who set nothing get identical behaviour except that
an [Authorize] 403 now reaches an explanation instead of a 404.

2.0.3 — version alignment.

No API change over 2.0.2. Rebuilt and republished alongside Ark.oAuth.Oidc 2.0.3 so the two halves
carry the same version. Consumers on 2.0.2 can upgrade with no code change; the notes for the
earlier versions apply unchanged and are kept below.

Worth knowing if you are upgrading the provider at the same time: 2.0.3 of Ark.oAuth.Oidc adds
back-channel logout, and this package does not host the receiving endpoint. An application that
wants its own cookie dropped when the IdP session ends registers a backchannel_logout_uri and
implements that endpoint itself — validate the posted logout_token against the provider's JWKS
(typ "logout+jwt", matching iss and aud, an events claim, no nonce), end the session it names, and
answer 200 or 204. Applications that register no URI are unaffected and keep behaving exactly as
they do on 2.0.2.

2.0.2 — version alignment.

No API change over 2.0.1. Rebuilt and republished alongside Ark.oAuth.Oidc 2.0.2 so the two halves
carry the same version. Consumers on 2.0.1 can upgrade with no code change; the 2.0.1 and 2.0.0
notes apply unchanged and are kept below.

2.0.1 — maintenance release.

No API change over 2.0.0. Rebuilt and republished alongside Ark.oAuth.Oidc 2.0.1 to keep the two
halves on the same version, and to carry the packaging fixes below. Consumers on 2.0.0 can upgrade
with no code change; the 2.0.0 notes apply unchanged and are kept below.

Packaging: the package icon (ark_logo.png) and the readme are packed at the root of the .nupkg, so
nuget.org and the Visual Studio package manager show both. The icon is referenced through
PackageIcon rather than the deprecated PackageIconUrl, and is included with an empty PackagePath so
it lands at the package root on a non-Windows build too.

2.0.0 — the standards release.

* AddArkOidcClient now configures ASP.NET Core's OpenID Connect and cookie handlers against the
  provider's discovery document. Real PKCE, state and nonce validation, JWKS rollover and silent
  refresh all come from the framework instead of being hand-rolled.
* Authority and ClientId are the only required settings — no pasted rsaPublic, no issuer/audience
  to mirror, no per-tenant key table to keep in step with rotation.
* AddArkOidcApi for protecting an API with bearer tokens from the same provider.
* Ark authorization claims (ark_claims) are projected onto the principal as role claims, so
  [Authorize(Roles = "...")] and policies work directly.
* GetArkAccessTokenAsync / WithArkTokenAsync read the current token per call, so a token refreshed
  by the cookie handler is picked up automatically.
* New services for the non-interactive flows: ArkSetupProbe (configuration vs. live metadata),
  ArkClientCredentials (client credentials grant with caching) and ArkRegistration (RFC 7591/7592).

Breaking / migration: the standard flow is now the default. Set ark_oauth_client:UseLegacyFlow to
true to keep the original cookie/bearer middleware while migrating — it does not validate state or
nonce and should be treated as a migration aid, not a supported configuration.

Packaging: the package no longer ships a sample appsettings file into consuming projects, and now
carries a readme, an SPDX license expression and a symbol package.
title: Ark Identity Client — OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect for ASP.NET Core
